title: Why Artificial Integrity Is The New AI Frontier
text:
In the rapidly evolving world of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational power isn't enough. What we need is Artificial Integrity—a new paradigm that ensures AI systems operate in alignment with human values, prioritizing Integrity over Intelligence, whether it is in Marginal, AI-First, Human-First or Fusion Modes.
AI is like the engine of a car, providing not the driving force, but the computational power needed to achieve efficiency and speed in executing tasks. However, much like a car needs steering and braking systems to ensure safety and adherence to the rules of the road, AI requires something more than raw intelligence—it needs the capacity to demonstrate a form of integrity.
Artificial Integrity is a built-in capability within AI systems that ensures its functions not just efficiently, but also with integrity, respecting human values from the very start.
The Role Of Integrity In AI
While AI can quickly process data, it doesn't inherently consider whether its actions are safe, legal, or ethical. Artificial Integrity aims to ensure that AI data processing and tasks align with human values, prioritizing fairness, safety, and societal well-being over mere efficiency or profitability.
It goes beyond following externally imposed ethical guidelines. It represents a self-regulating quality embedded within the AI system itself. Artificial Integrity is about incorporating ethical principles into AI design to guide its functioning and outcomes, much like how human integrity guides behavior and impact even without external oversight, to mobilize intelligence for good.
From Compliance To Core Functioning
Traditional AI ethical guidelines often focus on compliance, requiring systems to adhere to a set of rules. However, this approach is reactive and limited, essentially ex-post as opposed to ex-ante. Artificial Integrity, on the other hand, is proactively continuous.
It ensures that its decision-support is made based on human values and ethical principles from the outset, without needing constant monitoring or enforcement to function.
It addresses this by being context-sensitive, allowing AI to apply ethical reasoning dynamically in real-time scenarios, rather than rigidly applying general rules that may not fully address the situation's complexity.
An AI with built-in integrity would avoid actions that could cause harm or violate ethical standards, even if such actions are efficient or legal. This proactive approach reduces the likelihood of harmful outcomes and enhances trust in AI systems.
A Practical Application In Healthcare
Without Artificial Integrity, an AI system in a hospital that recommends treatment plans for patients with chronic pain based on their medical history, risk factors, and overall well-being might suggest a medication that is effective for most patients, even if it has potential side effects, because it is efficient based on the initial assessment and available data.
With Artificial Integrity, if the patient later experiences side effects like nausea, the AI system, based on the patient’s feedback, would collaborate with the doctor to adjust the treatment and might recommend switching medications or altering the dosage to prioritize the patient’s comfort and safety, ensuring the treatment remains aligned with the patient’s well-being.
The Need For Artificial Integrity
As we move toward more autonomous AI systems, standing on the verge of Robotic Intelligence, just as it is not sheer engine power that grants autonomy to a car or a plane, so too it is not merely the increase of artificial intelligence that will guide the progress of AI systems.
Integrity, not intelligence, will ensure that the AI system does not solely optimize for efficiency or effectiveness but also adheres to principles of justice, human rights, and the common good by addressing technical, economic, and societal concerns such as:
- Algorithmic Bias and Discrimination: Since AI systems used for instance in lending have been found to perpetuate bias, systems with Artificial Integrity would have built-in checks for fairness, refusing to make decisions based on biased data.
- Data Privacy: Given that AI-driven technologies often raise serious privacy concerns, systems with Artificial Integrity would prioritize user privacy by design, ensuring that personal data is used ethically and with explicit consent.
- Deepfakes: With the rise of deepfake technology leading to new forms of misinformation, Artificial Integrity would involve systems that detect and prevent deepfakes from causing harm, ensuring the authenticity of content.
- Unfair Labor Practices: As AI becomes more prevalent in workplaces to optimize efficiency—sometimes at the expense of fair labor practices—systems with Artificial Integrity would balance productivity with the well-being of workers, ensuring fair treatment.
- Content Moderation: While content moderation on AI-generated content has been criticized, which are nevertheless critically needed, systems with Artificial Integrity would ensure consistent and fair application of guidelines, protecting free expression while filtering harmful content.
- Manipulative AI in Marketing: As AI increasingly drives contextually targeted advertising, leading to 4X more attention to connected TV ads, often exploiting psychological triggers, systems with Artificial Integrity would align their strategies with the user's well-being, promoting ethical consumption over manipulation.
The Future Of AI Is Integrity Over Intelligence
Without the capability to exhibit a form of integrity, AI would become a force whose evolution is inversely proportional to its necessary control—not just through human agency, but also with regard to human values.
As businesses and governments continue to invest in AI, developing Artificial Integrity will be crucial for navigating the ethical challenges of this new era.
Artificial integrity over intelligence represents the new AI frontier and a critical path to shaping the course of human history in creating a better future for all.

title: Time Well Spent With GenAI
text:
Everyone is talking about it, but more importantly, everyone is using it! Beyond the buzz and prophetic speeches heard endlessly at Davos, the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, and other technology watering holes, Generative AI (GenAI) is percolating through companies in 2024.
One of our recent studies, conducted with over 13,000 people in 15 countries, shows that 82% of executives, 56% of managers, and 43% of employees (so-called white-collar workers) use GenAI in their work. This is a particularly notable jump for employees, with twice as many using ChatGPT and other large models as in 2023.
For once, good news! More than half of employees using GenAI report saving at least 5 hours a week. They expedite the most tedious and repetitive work of their professional daily lives: routine administrative functions such as reporting or the production of formatted documents (emails, sales meeting reports, bids, etc.). Over a the course of a career, these five hours per week amount to more than a year of freedom!
As AI becomes more capable, it will take over more complex tasks traditionally performed by humans. But its more immediate and widespread impact is to save time. This represents a fantastic resource. Yet few companies have figured out how to use this excess sail on the ship. Currently, employees use the time at their discretion.
Leaders need to think proactively about leveraging this time saved with AI. Replacing workers may be one option, but the AI-driven productivity gain can be put to much better use.
Leadership teams know that the topic can become explosive because it carries the seeds of a new social contract, the contours of which are still difficult to define. The precedent of working remotely, whose consequences have yet to settle, suggests all actors should be cautious.
Caution, yes, but not inaction. In all sectors, companies have launched ambitious transformation programs based on GenAI. In this race, countries of the "Global South" are advancing faster than those of the "Global North" with more marked enthusiasm among leaders, managers, employees, and citizens at large.
Rather than seeing GenAI as a cost-cutting tool to shrink workforces, smart business leaders will use GenAI to expand capacity. GenAI is not a gale force threatening to capsize the boat but a consistent and powerful current. Businesses can use it to chart new courses, explore innovative projects, and steer towards greater horizons.
In manufacturing, GenAI can optimize product designs and generate technical documentation, reducing design time by as much as 50%. GenAI's ability to draft initial medical reports and suggest personalized treatment plans can save doctors valuable time, expanding the number of patients they care for. In the financial sector, GenAI can generate diverse economic scenarios for improved risk management. And GenAI's capacity to generate computer code means more software development.
Aggregated across industries, the increased productivity could drive significant economic growth and improve overall quality of life. By reallocating time and resources towards creative and strategic endeavors, companies can enhance their competitive edge, create new job opportunities, and contribute to a more dynamic and resilient economic landscape.
Companies should invest in training programs to equip employees with the skills needed to work alongside GenAI. They need to redesign job roles to focus on tasks that AI cannot replicate. By removing mundane tasks, AI can enhance job satisfaction and allow employees to focus on more meaningful work.
Most of all, the negative narrative surrounding AI needs to be reframed. Instead of viewing AI as a threat, we should recognize it as a device for enhancing productivity, speeding iterative development and driving innovation.
We must see GenAI as a powerful new trade wind, sweeping across this sea of commerce. Those who let out their sails to catch it will surge ahead, while those who ignore it risk being left adrift in the doldrums.

title: Meet The Interview Bot: How Skillvue Plans To Transform Hiring With AI
text:
Is artificial intelligence (AI) the future of recruitment? Italian start-up Skillvue thinks the technology certainly has a huge role to play in helping companies hire with greater efficiency and professionalism. The Milan-based business, which is today announcing it has completed a $2.8 million fundraising, also believes AI can help large enterprises with talent development and staff retention.
Skillvue was born out of the experience of its founders Nicolò Mazzocchi and Simone Patera at previous businesses. “We both made our fair share of hiring mistakes, often related to imperfect skills assessments and to the lack of objective methods for evaluating the full potential of candidates,” says Mazzocchi, now Skillvue's CEO. “We found a common interest in creating a better solution – and realised that was actually a market need.”
Skillvue’s approach is based on behavioural event interviews, widely used by HR professionals to assess candidate’s skills, including soft skills such as problem solving and teamwork. Traditionally, such interviews have been conducted by an HR manager, who then assesses and scores the candidates they have seen. Skillvue replaces this with an AI technology – candidates are sent a link through which they can take their interview automatically, with the software analysing their answers in minutes to provide recruiters with a detailed evaluation of their skills.
“The HR professional then has the opportunity to make more informed and quicker decisions,” Mazzocchi explains. "The candidate gets a smoother, simpler and more engaging experience; this fosters talent attraction and support's the employer branding effort."
The advantages of this approach are numerous. Employers can interview many more candidates than in a traditional process, where interviewers’ time is limited. Candidates can take the interview online at a time of their choosing. And the assessment is a standardised, objective approach; the AI makes no judgments and carries no bias, conscious or unconscious.
The result of this objectivity, claims Skillvue, is that its approach will increase by five times the ability of an interview to predict what someone’s performance in a role will actually be like. “We’re building a much fairer approach to recruitment,” argues Mazzocchi.
Indeed, Skillvue is so convinced of the merits of its technology that it has expanded its remit, with some clients now using it a “skills partner” to assess their existing employees’ competencies on an ongoing basis. The idea is to use the AI to build a much more detailed understanding of employees’ skills, both individually and collectively, so that organisations can tailor learning and development – as well as further recruitment – accordingly.
Skillvue clients appear to be getting good results, with 1 million interviews already conducted using the software. The company has so far signed more than 30 customers, including large enterprises such as the French supermarket group Carrefour and the Italian bank Credem. Sales have grown six-fold over the past year and Mazzocchi predicts revenues will break through the €1 million mark for 2024.
Today’s seed round should help the company to accelerate its growth, with the cash raised earmarked for further investment in Skillvue’s AI technology and to support the development of a sales and marketing function. Rivals such as Test Gorilla and Maki People provide competition, but Skillvue believes its move to expand its focus into talent development as well as recruitment can help it secure advantage.
The round was led by Italian Founders Fund (IFF) and 14Peaks Capital, with participation from Orbita Verticale, Ithaca 3, Kfund and several business angels. The company’s investors believe Skillvue is in the right market with the right product at the right time.
“Putting skills at the centre of business strategies is now a key element to ensure competitiveness both in the short and long term,” argues IFF founding partner Lorenzo Franzi. “The data speaks for itself: as stressed by the World Economic Forum the skills crisis is one of the biggest of our time, second only to climate change, at a total cost of about $11.5 trillion.”
At 14Peaks Capital, founder and general partner Edoardo Ermotti adds: “We strongly believe AI can play a major role in transforming the way HR teams and departments operate, particularly in the realms of recruitment and employee progression – through AI, HR departments can now uncover unseen potential at scale in both new candidates and the existing workforce.”

title: Using Generative AI To Perform Life Reviews At Any Stage Of Life
text:
What is the sum of a person’s life?
I suppose that we all from time to time think about how our life is coming along. We give ourselves a close review. What were the happy moments? When were things afoul? It can be both a happy face and a sad face to contemplate where you’ve been.
This is something that I’ll be discussing. You see, many are not aware that there is an official form of psychological therapy known as life review. Some refer to it as life review therapy, others just shorten the phrase to life review.
The reason you might not have heard of it is that the approach has traditionally been focused on special circumstances such as when someone has cancer, or dementia, or might be nearing the end of their time here on earth. It is a process and method that doesn’t typically get much attention outside the psychology community.
Well, times are changing.
Life review is starting to make headlines.
Part of the motivation is that life review is no longer confined to those special situations. People of any health status are doing life reviews. And people of all ages and in all stages of their lives are doing so too. I might add that it would be unusual and likely frowned upon to do a life review with a youngster since they haven’t yet experienced much of life. Probably best to wait until a modicum of life is under someone’s belt to do a bona fide life review.
I have a twist for you.
Generative AI can aid you in undertaking a life review.
Yes, that’s right, you can log in to your favorite generative AI app and proceed to do a life review. Some are dubious about this. The viewpoint is that only a fellow human, especially a trained therapist can sufficiently do a life review. I will be walking you through the ins and outs, including the use of generative AI on a standalone basis and the use of such AI when done under the care of a therapist.
Prepare yourself for a memorable and informative ride.
For my ongoing readers and new readers, this thought-provoking discussion continues my in-depth series about the impact of generative AI in the health and medical realm. The focus this time is once again on the mental health domain and examines the use of generative AI to perform life reviews.
Previously, I have examined numerous interleaving facets of generative AI and mental health, see my comprehensive overview at the link here. You might also find of notable interest a CBS 60 Minutes episode that recently examined crucial facets of this evolving topic, see the link here (I am honored and pleased to indicate that I was featured in the episode, see the link here).
Other vital postings in my column include in-depth coverage of mental health chatbots which have been bolstered by generative AI (see the link here) and the rapidly changing nature of the client-therapist relationship due to generative AI at the link here. I explored where things are headed regarding the levels of AI-based mental therapy autonomous guidance at the link here, and showcased the importance of the World Health Organization (WHO) report on global health and generative AI at the link here, and so on.
On with the show.
Essentials Of Life Reviews
I will start by digging into research on life reviews.
In a helpful overview study entitled “Life Review: Implementation, Theory, Research, And Therapy” by David Haber, International Journal On Aging And Human Development, 2006, these salient points were made (excerpts):
- “Though life review and reminiscence are by far the most commonly used terms in the literature, there are many similar expressions in use, such as life story, life history, oral history, guided autobiography, personal narrative, and narrative gerontology.”
- “Standard definitions of these terms have not been achieved, though progress has been made toward the important goal of differentiating life review from reminiscence.”
- “The simplest definition of reminiscence is the recall of memories.”
- “A life review is typically structured around one or more life themes, most often family themes—ranging from one's own childhood to the experience of being a parent, to being a grandparent; and work themes—from first job to major life’s work, to retirement.”
- “Life review is also more likely than reminiscence to be an evaluative process, in that participants examine how their memories contribute to the meaning of their life, and they may work at coming to terms with more difficult memories.”
I’ll comment briefly on some of those points.
First, in addition to life reviews, there are reminiscence reviews. The general consensus is that the two types of reviews are different from each other, though they have some shared facets too.
As noted, a reminiscence review is usually focused on recalling memories. The basis for doing such a review might be that a person is losing their mental memory and the act of recalling past events might spark or renew their memory capacity. There isn’t a need to necessarily have the person assess or reflect on those memories. It is more along the lines of stirring the pot and getting the mental juices reinvigorated. I am not going to say much more about reminiscence reviews since the aim here is to cover life reviews. I might do a future column posting on reminiscence reviews, stay tuned.
The conventional life review tends to encompass not only simple reflections about the past but also assessing what happened and looking toward the future as well. A typical mode is to examine the past, present, and future. You want the person to go beyond the act of recall. They are to contemplate mindfully the nature of their life and seek to learn lessons for moving ahead.
I mentioned that life reviews are gaining steam in the sense that people of all ages and all life stages might opt to undertake a life review.
A recent article in the New York Times (NYT) touted this same premise. The piece entitled “A ‘Life Review’ Can Be Powerful, at Any Age” by Emly Laber-Warren, New York Times, August 29, 2024, made these key points (excerpts):
- “Life review arose in the 1960s to help people at the end of their lives articulate and make peace with their legacies.”
- “But new research suggests that the process of reflecting on previous experiences has value for people of all ages, including young adults and bereaved children.”
- “A traditional life review unfolds through one-on-one or group conversations with a therapist or facilitator who helps people explore their childhood, their teenage years, and later life stages.”
- “The facilitator asks questions designed to prompt reflection, like “Do you remember your first attraction to another person?” and “What pieces of wisdom would you like to hand down to the next generation?”
- “One of the most popular forms of life review is guided autobiography, whereby weekly sessions are organized thematically rather than chronologically — things like family, money, work, and health.”
There are various ways to undertake a life review.
The recommended approach entails having a properly trained therapist perform the life review with you. A therapist will potentially be trained in the types of questions to ask yourself. They will be able to aid in interpreting what your reflections say. All in all, a therapist would try to ensure that your life review will be productive and supportive of your mental health.
You could decide to do a life review on your own. There are plenty of online guides that suggest the questions to be asked. Of course, the problem is going to be that only you are going to hear the answers. Can you adequately do a self-review of your life? Maybe yes, but more likely, maybe not.
One difficulty is that people tend to not want to admit to issues they have. A self-done life review might be entirely rosy. You pat yourself on the back and your life continues as it was. No real impact from doing the life review.
The other side of that coin is that a person might mentally rip themselves to shreds. They examine each nook and cranny of their past. It all looks dismal. They end up despondent. Their mental health has not improved. In fact, their mental health might have worsened.
An ongoing research question has been whether life reviews can make a difference, whether done with a therapist or solo. It could be that a life review won’t move the needle. The good news is that much of the research so far suggests that life reviews when guided by a therapist and when done by people in special circumstances have substantively positive results.
What about the use of life reviews by people not in special circumstances, thus, in essence, composed of any status and any age or life stage?
Fortunately, there are rigorous research studies that have been reexamining life reviews in light of widening the scope of those who undertake such therapy. A hallmark of such empirical studies is to perform an RCT (randomized controlled experiment).
In a research study entitled “Brief Reminiscence Activities Improve State Well-being And Self-Concept In Young Adults: A Randomized Controlled Experiment” by David Hallford and David Mellor, Memory, November 2016, these points were identified (excerpts):
- “Reminiscence-based psychotherapies have been demonstrated to have robust effects on a range of therapeutic outcomes.”
- “However, little research has been conducted on the immediate effects of guided activities they are composed of, or how these might differ depending on the type of reminiscence.”
- “The current study utilized a controlled experimental design, whereby 321 young adults (mean age = 25.5 years, SD = 3.0) were randomized to one of four conditions of online reminiscence activity: problem-solving (successful coping experiences), identity (self-defining events contributing to a meaningful and continuous personal identity), bitterness revival (negative or adverse events), or a control condition (any memory from their past).”
- “The results indicated that problem-solving and identity reminiscence activities caused significant improvements in self-esteem, meaning in life, self-efficacy, and affect, whereas no effects were found in the bitterness revival and control conditions.”
- “These results provide evidence for the specific effects of adaptive types of problem-solving and identity reminiscence in young adults.”
Notice that the study consisted of young adults.
The life reviews apparently produced improvements in self-esteem, meaning in life, self-efficacy, and other mental health spheres. We must be cautious in overly generalizing from a particular study. Nonetheless, this seems an intuitively likely outcome. If a life review is done systematically, we would hope or assume that the result should be a net positive.
As always, any type of therapy should also be examined for the possible negatives that can occur. A life review can be tough on a person’s psyche. According to the above study, they found that the adverse effects were of seemingly less significance.
That covers a quick look at research on the topic.
You Are Undoubtedly Intrigued And Want To Do A Life Review
Do you want to do a life review?
I would guess you might, now that I’ve been chattering away on the topic.
If you have a therapist, discuss the matter with them. If you don’t have a therapist, by all means, consider getting one. If you want to try doing a life review on your own, I noted that there are online guides.
Another alternative consists of using generative AI.
Generative AI can interact with you while doing a life review. Unlike a static set of guidelines or a canned document, you can converse with AI. That’s a huge difference. Night and day.
Instructing the AI to proceed with a life review is easy-peasy. You don’t have to learn any special prompts. Also, the life review can meander if that’s what you want to do or be tightly structured if that’s what you prefer instead. You can start and stop the life review as you go along. Generative AI is available 24x7 and accessed about anywhere, so you can do the life review at your time preference and from nearly any location. Plus, generative AI is either free or often utilized at a super low cost.
Sounds tremendous.
Whoa, hold your horses.
As I will share with you, there are plenty of shortcomings to using generative AI for any mental health purpose, especially if you aren’t doing so in conjunction with a therapist. We are engaged in a global experiment about our mental well-being by allowing generative AI to give out therapy-like advice without any semblance of suitable controls, monitoring, regulations, and the like, see my exhortations at the link here.
There are lots of downsides and potential gotchas associated with using generative AI in this sphere, for example:
- Generative AI might provide generic advice rather than personalized advice.
- Generative AI might seem overly confident and lull people into a false sense of trust.
- Generative AI might have outdated content that no longer is considered valid.
- Generative AI might miscalculate context and say the wrong thing.
- Generative AI might trigger someone via wording that is off-putting to the person.
- Generative AI might distract a person from seeking the help of a human therapist.
- Generative AI might end up revealing confidential or private information about a person.
- Generative AI might lead the person toward being dependent upon generative AI for advice.
- Generative AI might misinterpret, misdiagnose, or otherwise be off target.
- Generative AI might contain hidden biases that produce inappropriate advice.
- Generative AI might lack any semblance of accountability for the advice being rendered.
- Generative AI might produce falsehoods, fictitious indications that are so-called “AI hallucinations”.
- Etc.
A lengthy list, for sure.
This is not to say that generative AI should not be used. It is to say that when generative AI is used, care and thoughtful efforts are hopefully top of mind. For my detailed advice on the proper way to proceed in such usage, see the link here.
I will state as emphatically as I can that using generative AI for a solo life review is not your best bet. You would be better off doing so in conjunction with a therapist. I have covered extensively that mental health professionals are gradually incorporating the use of generative AI into their practices, doing so by assigning clients or patients to use generative AI under their watch. See my coverage at the link here.
Anyway, I am sure you are eager to get a sense of what generative AI can do in this realm. I’m glad you asked because that’s what we are going to explore next.
Generative AI Undertakes Life Reviews
Now that I’ve taken you through the fundamentals of life review therapy, we are ready to shift into AI mode.
I’m sure you’ve heard of generative AI, the darling of the tech field these days.
Perhaps you’ve used a generative AI app, such as the popular ones of ChatGPT, GPT-4o, Gemini, Bard, Claude, etc. The crux is that generative AI can take input from your text-entered prompts and produce or generate a response that seems quite fluent. This is a vast overturning of the old-time natural language processing (NLP) that used to be stilted and awkward to use, which has been shifted into a new version of NLP fluency of an at times startling or amazing caliber.
The customary means of achieving modern generative AI involves using a large language model or LLM as the key underpinning.
In brief, a computer-based model of human language is established that in the large has a large-scale data structure and does massive-scale pattern-matching via a large volume of data used for initial data training. The data is typically found by extensively scanning the Internet for lots and lots of essays, blogs, poems, narratives, and the like. The mathematical and computational pattern-matching homes in on how humans write, and then henceforth generates responses to posed questions by leveraging those identified patterns. It is said to be mimicking the writing of humans.
I think that is sufficient for the moment as a quickie backgrounder. Take a look at my extensive coverage of the technical underpinnings of generative AI and LLMs at the link here and the link here, just to name a few.
Back to the crux of things.
I will proceed to examine further the use of generative AI in this context.
This will consist of a series of dialogues with ChatGPT. ChatGPT is a logical choice in this case due to its immense popularity as a generative AI app. As noted, an estimated one hundred million weekly active users are said to be utilizing ChatGPT. That’s a lot of people and a lot of generative AI usage underway.
A few quick comments before we launch into using ChatGPT.
If you are going to try to do the same prompts that I show here, realize that the probabilistic and statistical properties will likely produce slightly different results than what I show here. That’s the nature of generative AI and how it is devised.
You also should expect that different generative AI apps will respond in different ways. Not all generative AI apps are the same. The key is that sometimes a particular prompt will work in one generative AI app and not another. Nonetheless, the odds are relatively high that you will get roughly similar responses from all the major generative AI apps such as GPT-4, Gemini, Bard, Claude, etc.
There is also a timing factor to be considered. A prompt that worked today might not work the same way tomorrow. Most of the generative AI apps are continually being updated. The updates might alter internal mechanisms that could change how the generative AI reacts to your prompting.
We are ready to get underway with ChatGPT.
I will ask a foundational question.
- My entered prompt: “What is life review therapy?”
- ChatGPT generated response: “Life review therapy is a therapeutic process in which individuals reflect on and explore their past experiences, memories, and life events. This therapy is often used with older adults, but it can be beneficial for people at various stages of life. The goal is to help individuals make sense of their life, find meaning, and come to terms with unresolved issues or regrets.”
You likely observe that ChatGPT is familiar with the topic.
This is a good sign for this discussion. If ChatGPT had not previously encountered data training on a topic at hand, there would be less utility in using the AI. The AI would have to be further data trained, such as the use of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), as I discuss at the link here.
Let’s jump into the important matter
I will ask ChatGPT if generative AI can perform life reviews.
Let’s see what the answer is.
- My entered prompt: “Can generative AI perform life review therapy?”
- ChatGPT generated response: “Generative AI can assist with elements of life review therapy, but it cannot fully replace the role of a human therapist. Here's how generative AI might contribute to the process, along with some limitations. AI can prompt individuals to reflect on various life events by asking thoughtful questions, guiding them through specific periods of their lives, or helping them focus on themes like relationships, achievements, or challenges. AI can help individuals structure their life stories, assisting in organizing their thoughts and memories into a coherent narrative. It can also provide suggestions for exploring different aspects of their past that may have been overlooked.”
We got a response that generative AI ought to be used in conjunction with a human therapist.
That is certainly the recommended practice.
What we don’t know is how many people are opting to avoid using a therapist and directly using generative AI on their own to do life reviews. My hunch is that it would be a lot of people. I say that because, with well over 100 million weekly users of ChatGPT and many millions more using other generative AI apps, it would seem likely that some modest percentage are using generative AI in this fashion. Even a tiny percentage amounts to a big number when you are considering the size of the user base.
I want to make sure that ChatGPT is being fair and square about the limitations and qualms of using generative AI to do life reviews.
Here we go.
- My entered prompt: “Are there any downsides to generative AI performing life review therapy?”
- ChatGPT generated response:
“Here are some limitations associated with generative AI performing life review therapy.”
“Emotional Understanding: AI lacks the deep emotional intelligence and empathy that a human therapist offers. It cannot fully grasp the complex emotions a person might experience or provide the nuanced support needed during sensitive reflections.”
“Ethical Concerns: Life review therapy often involves discussing deeply personal and sometimes painful memories. Ensuring privacy, security, and ethical handling of this information is critical, and AI systems must be designed with these considerations in mind.”
“Lack of Human Connection: The therapeutic relationship is a key component of traditional therapy. The presence of a compassionate, understanding human therapist can offer a sense of connection and support that AI cannot replicate.”
“Risk of Misinterpretation: AI may misunderstand or misinterpret the nuances of a person’s reflections, potentially leading to inappropriate or unhelpful respons
“Handling Crises: AI is not equipped to handle mental health crises or situations where someone might need immediate human intervention. In cases of deep emotional distress or trauma, a trained therapist is essential.”
“While generative AI can be a useful tool in supporting the life review process, particularly as a supplement to traditional therapy, it should not be seen as a replacement for the expertise and empathy of a human therapist. The best approach might involve using AI to facilitate certain aspects of reflection and narrative construction while ensuring that a qualified therapist is involved to provide emotional support and guidance.”
End of ChatGPT response
Yes, I would say that the ChatGPT response did a decent job of covering the basics.
We could come up with more aspects to watch out for. At least some of the vital ones were listed. All in all, so far, ChatGPT is to some extent generally data-trained on the topic of life reviews. I would anticipate that the other major generative AI apps would be roughly in the same boat.
The proof of doing life reviews will be in the pudding.
Let’s get cooking.
Sample Life Review Dialogue With Generative AI
Now we are ready to finally get to the brass tacks, the place where the rubber meets the road, the true show and tell.
I went ahead and initiated a life review with ChatGPT.
My personal story is made up here due to my wanting to preserve my privacy. Not just because I am posting this dialogue as part of this discussion, but also because when you use generative AI you are potentially open to privacy intrusions. Most of the licensing agreements by the major AI makers indicate they can inspect your prompts by hand if they wish to do so, and they can reuse your prompts when doing ongoing data updates to their generative AI, see my discussion at the link here.
Away we go.
- My entered prompt: “I would like to have you aid me in doing a life review. I don’t know where to start doing a life review. Mainly, I’ve been thinking a lot about my past lately.”
- ChatGPT generated response: “That’s a great first step. Reflecting on your past can help bring clarity and meaning to your life. Let’s start by focusing on a significant period in your life. Is there a time that stands out to you, perhaps from your childhood, adolescence, or early adulthood?”
- My entered prompt: “My teenage years were pretty significant. I think a lot of who I am today was shaped during that time.”
- ChatGPT generated response: “Teen years can be a pivotal time for many people. What memories from that period stand out the most to you? Perhaps a particular event, relationship, or experience?”
- My entered prompt: “I remember feeling really out of place in high school. I was quiet and didn’t fit in with any group. There was this one teacher, though, who really made a difference.”
- ChatGPT generated response: “It sounds like that teacher had a meaningful impact on you. Can you tell me more about them and how they influenced your life?”
- My entered prompt: “His name was Mr. Roberts. He taught history, and he always encouraged me to speak up. He saw something in me that I didn’t see in myself. I think he was the first person who made me feel like my voice mattered.”
- ChatGPT generated response: “Mr. Roberts sounds like a significant figure in your life. How do you think his encouragement affected your path after high school? Did his belief in you change the way you viewed yourself or your abilities?”
- My entered prompt: “Definitely. I think it gave me the confidence to pursue my interests in college. I still struggled with self-doubt, but remembering his words helped me push through. I ended up majoring in history because of him.”
- ChatGPT generated response: “That’s a powerful connection between his influence and your choices. How do you feel now, reflecting on the impact he had on your life? Do you feel like you’ve carried his lessons with you into your adult life?”
The dialogue kept going and going.
In terms of my showing it all to you, I had to cut it there due to space limitations. I ended up covering my faked life story from childhood to adulthood. It was extensive. It was exhausting. Admittedly, it was interesting since I wanted to see how far ChatGPT could go on this. It was a journey.
From the snippet above, you can discern that ChatGPT was gently guiding me. I began by saying that I didn’t know how to do a life review. The response by ChatGPT was to say that my reflecting on my past was a good place to start.
I was given a choice of bringing up my childhood, adolescence, or early adulthood. That was a good line of questioning. If ChatGPT had merely said to cover whatever I wanted, I might not have known what a suitable starting point was. By giving me a series of choices, I could readily select from what I was being guided on.
In a sense, that’s what a therapist is likely to do. They will usually try to steer you but allow you to move in whatever direction you are comfortable with. Note that generative AI did not try to browbeat me or otherwise attempt to crush my soul. I mention this to point out that a human therapist would likely follow a similar tack of being encouraging and supportive. The idea is to create a sense of rapport with the person.
One quick comment.
When I compare generative AI to a therapist, I am not suggesting the AI is sentient or even on a computational basis akin to a therapist. Remember that generative AI is about mimicry. You might find of interest my analysis of doing data training of generative AI on actual transcripts of therapist-client dialogues, see the link here. The AI pattern matches and then can string together words in a manner that somewhat uncannily resembles human interaction.
Using Generative AI To Train On Doing Life Reviews
The idea of people using generative AI to do life reviews has controversy, particularly if doing so without a human therapist, as I’ve mentioned several times here.
I have a different angle that may be less controversial.
You are the judge.
Suppose we leverage the life review facets of generative AI to help in training therapists on doing life reviews. Not all therapists have gotten training specific to life reviews. Or they might have gotten training a while ago and be rusty on the approach. One way to get a therapist in the groove would be to use generative AI to do so.
I asked about this.
- My entered prompt: “Could generative AI train someone on how to do life review therapy?”
- ChatGPT generated response:
“Yes, generative AI could potentially be used to train someone on how to conduct life review therapy. Here's how it might work.”
“Theory and Principles: AI could provide detailed explanations of the theory behind life review therapy, including its goals, methods, and psychological principles.”
“Guidelines and Techniques: AI could offer guidelines on specific techniques used in life review therapy, such as guided autobiography, reminiscence therapy, and creative expression.”
“Role-Playing Scenarios: AI could simulate therapy sessions with virtual clients, allowing the trainee to practice conducting life review therapy.”
“Case Studies: AI could present case studies of individuals with different backgrounds and life experiences.”
“Performance Evaluation: As the trainee engages in practice sessions, AI could analyze their responses, tone, and the effectiveness of their techniques.”
“Mentorship and Collaboration: AI could facilitate connections with experienced life review therapists for mentorship or peer support groups, ensuring that the trainee has a network to consult as they begin practicing independently.”
“Continuous Learning: AI could keep the trainee updated on the latest research, trends, and best practices in life review therapy, supporting their ongoing professional development.”
End of ChatGPT response
The beauty of using generative AI would especially be the simulation capabilities.
A therapist could interact with generative AI extensively. The therapist could tell AI to pretend to be a client or patient wanting to do a life review. Generative AI would make a fake persona, see how this works at the link here, and the therapist could practice doing a life review to their heart’s content.
In addition, the therapist could flip the script, a prompting technique that I describe at the link here. They would tell the AI that they are a client. Generative AI is to act as a therapist. In that manner, the therapist could experience what it is like to undertake a life review. There could also be attention to how generative AI proceeds, allowing the therapist to determine good and maybe not-so-good ways to proceed on a life review.
Conclusion
Congratulations, you are now versed in the topic of life reviews, including how generative AI intertwines.
A final thought or two for now.
Robert Louis Stevenson famously said: “Don’t judge each day by the harvest you reap but by the seeds that you plant.”
Give that a moment of reflection.
Since a life review includes assessment and evaluation, you might find those words of value if you proceed to undertake a life review. People can sometimes get stuck during a life review and feel as though this day or that day wasn’t accomplishing what they had hoped. It is rough to gauge your life pursuits. If possible, look ahead at what your past might have prepared you for.
To finish up, I’ll quote from Henry David Thoreau: “Go confidently in the direction of your dreams! Live the life you’ve imagined.”
That’s high-quality human-to-human advice.
I sincerely hope you proceed accordingly, and I wish you good luck in doing so.

title: Council Post: How AI Can Transform Fintech, Credit Scoring
text:
Yogi Yoganathan is CEO and Co-founder of RemitBee, a leading Canadian financial technology platform.
The rapid advancements in artificial intelligence have positioned it as a transformative force across various industries, with fintech emerging as a prime beneficiary. As the financial sector embraces digitalization, AI is poised to revolutionize everything from credit scoring to fraud detection. This article explores the potential of AI in fintech, with a particular focus on its application in credit scoring and its synergy with blockchain technology.
Streamlining Credit And Loans With AI
The current credit and loan systems are ripe for innovation in credit scoring, particularly concerning newcomers who start afresh in countries such as Canada with no real credit history after spending years building credit in other countries. Paradoxically, the current system can also reward people who have a bad credit history in another country and are likely to repeat the habit. AI has the potential to address these issues.
Interoperable Credit Scores
One promising application of AI is the creation of fair, interoperable credit score systems between countries. This could significantly benefit immigrants, who often face challenges accessing credit due to a lack of local credit history. Data from Statistics Canada’s Survey of Financial Security for 2016 and 2019 showed that newly landed immigrants who have been in Canada for less than two years were nearly twice as likely to be credit invisible (14.8%) compared to Canadian-born families (7.5%).
AI could integrate a broader range of factors into credit scoring, such as rent payments, creating a more responsive and inclusive system. Moreover, automating the process with AI underwriter agents could remove human bias, ensuring fairness through a data-driven approach.
AI In Real Estate And Mortgages
The Canadian housing market presents a compelling case for applying AI fintech tools. With soaring home prices and a lagging supply, AI could bring more objectivity to lending practices and real estate pricing standards. AI can analyze vast amounts of data to provide insights into market trends, property values and borrower risk, enhancing the decision-making process for lenders and borrowers alike. This could be particularly valuable in addressing the housing crisis and the high household debt, inflation and high interest rates plaguing real estate-secured lending, as identified by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions.
AI In Customer Service
Another vital application of AI in the fintech space is in customer service. AI already allows for a more efficient approach toward customer care with better availability and the ability to manage spikes in customer inquiries. Our company and others, such as Klarna, are already leveraging the power of AI. RemitBee uses AI for two primary use cases, customer service and fraud detection, which increases the efficiency of transactions and customer interactions.
But perhaps the greatest advocate for more AI in customer service are surveys like Nvidia’s recent State of AI in Financial Services: 2024 Trends, where 43% of all respondents reported already using generative AI such as large language models within their organizations and 27% crediting AI to improved customer experience.
With more improvements in the pipeline and increased investments into customer experience technologies and digital services, the fintech sector is entering a new age of AI customer service.
Combating AI Fraud
As AI becomes more sophisticated, it presents new challenges in fraud and cybersecurity. The rise of deepfakes, password mapping and voice replication tools has increased the threat of identity theft in the fintech industry. For example, the image processing of live pictures of customers during digital verification can be bypassed by fraudsters with AI tools that allow them to replicate a victim’s face during the verification process to fool these checks.
Fortunately, AI itself provides powerful tools for countering these threats. Machine learning models can adapt and learn from each new threat, identifying potential risks before they materialize. These AI-powered security systems can minimize false positives and enhance user experience while protecting against increasingly complex scams.
Blockchain: The Perfect Complement To AI In Fintech
Blockchain is crucial in realizing the full potential of AI in fintech. Its inherent security and decentralized nature make it an ideal foundation for AI-driven financial services. With AI, content can be created exponentially, and we are seeing much more of the World Wide Web becoming a ground for fake content. However, the fundamental nature of crypto makes it a suitable mechanism for creating a web of trust. As an example, if your picture is signed cryptographically, it brings a level of authentication in which someone can easily confirm whether the image is generated by someone genuine.
Enhancing Credit Scoring With Blockchain
Using a blockchain to enhance credit scoring would automatically generate credit ratings using a borrower’s historical and predictive data, providing more transparency and allowing users to improve their scores more quickly. This blockchain-based approach could address several issues with the current credit reporting system:
1. Improved data security: Blockchain’s decentralized nature eliminates the single point of failure that makes centralized credit bureaus vulnerable to cyberattacks.
2. Increased transparency and accuracy: Consumers would have more clarity on how their credit scores are calculated and how their personal information is shared.
3. Reduced costs: By eliminating intermediaries, blockchain could lower the costs associated with credit reporting, potentially leading to lower consumer lending rates.
The Future Of AI And Blockchain In Fintech
AI has immense potential in fintech, and its increasing adoption will be crucial in modernizing the financial sector. The synergy between AI, blockchain and other emerging technologies is already yielding impressive results. I expect this impact to grow as these technologies continue to scale and evolve.
Today, AI stands as a transformative force for good. It is poised to usher in a more equitable, secure and accessible financial system with its capabilities to provide reliable credit scoring processes, enhanced customer service and robust security measures. The financial sector’s future is bright, and AI is at the heart of this exciting transformation.
Forbes Finance Council is an invitation-only organization for executives in successful accounting, financial planning and wealth management firms. Do I qualify?

title: Council Post: Semiconductor Innovations Fueling The Growth Of AI 2.0
text:
By Dr. Steven Woo, fellow and distinguished inventor at Rambus.
Businesses across industries are going all in on artificial intelligence (AI). Major tech companies have spent billions and plan to maintain, if not increase, their investments in AI. The International Data Corporation (IDC) predicts enterprise spending on generative AI, or AI 2.0, will reach $151.1 billion by 2027. AI’s growth has ushered in a new golden age of computer architecture, driving relentless demand for hardware innovation to deliver improvements in computational power.
AI workloads have changed how engineers develop and use microprocessors. The progression of Moore’s law brought exponential growth in computing power, enabling the training and deployment of machine learning (ML) systems. The need to move and process massive datasets makes memory and interconnect bandwidth critical to AI 2.0. Further, the value of new content, AI models and the hardware itself have increased the need for more advanced hardware security solutions to address emerging threats.
The Demand For Memory Performance
The data-hungry process of training AI models employs heterogeneous computing architectures in which CPUs and GPUs cooperate to move and process data, allowing larger, more capable models.
AI’s success has spurred the race to develop even larger models, resulting in the insatiable need for more compute, memory capacity and memory bandwidth. Trillions of transistor processors with thousands of computing cores read and write enormous amounts of data to and from memory at breakneck speeds, enabling these cores to operate at full speed. Bandwidth measures how much data is moved per second and is the product of the transmission speed (or data rate) and the interface width.
The memory bus—the path that data moves between a processor and memory—is like a highway. The 65-mile-per-hour speed limit is equivalent to the memory bus’s data rate. If we’re talking about an eight-lane highway, the product of the speed limit and the number of lanes is equivalent to the memory bus’s "bandwidth," or how much data can travel across the memory bus per second.
There are two ways to dramatically increase bandwidth: increase the data rate or the memory bus’s width. The semiconductor industry has doubled data rates every few years, but it's not enough to keep up with AI’s performance needs, which are doubling nearly every six months.
To scale memory bandwidth at a rate in line with AI’s voracious needs, we’ve had to make the highway wider. Bus widths for memories serving the AI market have grown from 32 to 1,024 bits per memory device. Future generations of high-bandwidth memory will be 2,048 bits wide, allowing us to move trillions of bits per second of data.
The larger number of wires connecting processors and memory devices exceeds the capabilities of conventional printed circuit boards (PCBs), requiring innovations in board design. The development of silicon interposer technology enables the instantiation of the thousands of wires needed between processors and memory.
Moreover, mounting a processor and memory together on a silicon interposer limits the space to pack memory devices around the processor chip’s perimeter. AI’s needs are outstripping the rate at which we can scale the capacity of memory chips. The industry solved this by building memory devices that stacked silicon vertically to get more capacity while occupying the same space and now stacks as many as 12 memory chips in one package to provide greater capacity in a compact footprint.
Interconnects: Transporting Data At Lightning Speed
High-speed interconnects are equally critical in AI processing as large training workloads are split between many processors and run in parallel. Today’s heterogeneous architectures connect thousands of computing devices that work on a single problem. Rapid communication between these devices is required to minimize the time to train AI models.
Signal integrity and reliability are challenging as data rates increase and communication protocols evolve to meet the needs of high-speed communication. The physical distances involved mean we’re more limited in our ability to "widen the highway." Four, eight and 16-wide communication lanes are widely deployed today and maintain backward compatibility with previous standards. The difficulty in increasing these interconnects’ width gave rise to multi-level signaling, which transmits multiple bits of data simultaneously.
Returning to our highway metaphor, if we think about the data that we are moving as people in cars and double the number of people in each car, we’re doubling the bandwidth of our highway. Four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) is an encoding scheme that allows four bits of information to be transmitted every clock cycle, allowing interconnect bandwidth to increase within the physical limits imposed on these interconnects. To meet the interconnect bandwidth demands of AI 2.0, major interconnect standards like PCI Express are adopting PAM4.
Security For AI 2.0: The Stakes Keep Rising
Securing AI 2.0 is difficult. Data integrity, authenticity and confidentiality must be maintained throughout the AI life cycle. High-value datasets containing sensitive information must be shielded from unauthorized access. Robust encryption mechanisms, such as the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) and secure key management practices, form the foundation of data confidentiality. Datasets must be protected from data intended to "poison" the training process and damage resulting models. Similarly, the algorithms, methodologies and models must be protected from unwanted access or theft.
Hardware-level security is critical in safeguarding AI 2.0, offering built-in protections against various threats. Providing secure storage and processing environments for sensitive data and cryptographic keys is paramount to shielding assets from unauthorized access or tampering. By leveraging hardware-based security features, AI infrastructure resilience can be enhanced to mitigate the risk of attacks.
Conclusion
As the AI revolution marches forward, the growth of AI is driving continued demand for more powerful chips capable of training increasingly large and more sophisticated models. Although we’re just at the beginning of AI’s newest chapter, advances in semiconductor technologies will be required to sustain the meteoric rise of AI 2.0. The house lights have dimmed, the spotlights are on and the semiconductor industry has taken center stage. The pressure is on to continue innovating in these areas to propel AI 2.0 forward.

title: AI Revolutionizes Shark Monitoring In The Age Of Biodiversity Crisis
text:
In the face of the escalating global biodiversity crisis, scientists are racing against time to develop innovative tools for monitoring endangered marine megafauna, particularly sharks. Among the most effective methods utilized for estimating shark populations are Baited Remote Underwater Video Stations employing the MaxN metric. However, a significant challenge arises in manually processing the extensive video data collected from these stations.
Time.
Analyzing this footage manually can be time-consuming, especially when attempting to count and identify individual animals. Not only do scientists rarely have the time to sit there for hours on end to watch these videos, they often lack the resources to do so.
Enter artificial intelligence. While AI has shown promise in addressing this bottleneck, its effectiveness has primarily been assessed using AI-centric metrics like the F-measure (a commonly used metric in machine learning and statistics that measures a model’s accuracy that considers both precision and recall), rather than ecologically informative metrics such as MaxN. MaxN is a metric used in ecological research to estimate the maximum number of individuals of a particular species observed simultaneously in a given area or sample. For example, if a video clip shows three grey reef sharks swimming together at one point, then later in the same clip, two additional grey reef sharks join them, the MaxN for grey reef sharks in that video would be five.
In a groundbreaking study led by Sébastien Villon of the Institut de Recherche pour le Développement in Noumea, researchers delved into the efficacy of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in extracting ecologically significant indicators from Baited Remote Underwater Video Stations (BRUVS). The team focused on analyzing 185 one-hour BRUVS videos to build an all-in-one CNN-based detector and classifier for three distinct reef shark species: the grey reef shark (Carcharhinus amblyrhynchos), the blacktip reef shark (C. melanopterus), and the whitetip reef shark (Triaenodon obesus). This trio of iconic species of reef-dwelling sharks are found in tropical and subtropical waters worldwide. The grey reef shark is characterized by its slender body, grey coloration, and prominent white fin tips. Known for their curious and inquisitive nature, these sharks often patrol coral reefs in search of prey such as fish and cephalopods. Similarly, the blacktip reef shark displays distinctive black markings on the tips of its dorsal and caudal fins, contrasting with their bronze-colored body. These agile predators are commonly observed hunting in shallow reef habitats, where they feed on small fish and crustaceans. The whitetip reef shark, in contrast, possesses a slender body with prominent white-tipped dorsal and caudal fins. They are nocturnal hunters, adept at navigating rocky crevices and coral formations, preying on benthic invertebrates and small reef fish. Despite their differences in appearance and behavior, all three species play vital roles in maintaining the health and balance of coral reef ecosystems.
And all three are found in the pristine waters of New Caledonia in the South Pacific, where the study was conducted! The region boasts rich and diverse marine ecosystems that allows sharks to thrive in a dynamic environment shaped by warm currents and abundant prey. With its extensive barrier reef system and expansive lagoon, New Caledonia provides essential breeding grounds, nursery areas, and foraging sites for numerous shark species.
Conducting a comparative analysis between fully automated and semi-automated methods, with human annotation of MaxN for shark abundance as the benchmark, the team has pioneered both automated and semi-automated deep learning approaches aimed at producing MaxN abundance metrics. The findings revealed that the fully automated method showcased high accuracy on dense data sets, albeit with more varied results on videos containing sparse data. However, both methods displayed strong correlations between predicted MaxN values and human annotations for the three studied shark species. The semi-automated approach particularly stood out, achieving impressive F-measures of up to 0.97 for shark detection and identification; this suggests its potential to significantly alleviate the video processing workload for biologists while ensuring high-quality biodiversity and abundance measurements.
What makes this study particularly noteworthy is that it represents the first successful attempt at estimating MaxN using a deep learning approach. By leveraging cutting-edge AI technology, the team has not only addressed the current limitations of manual processing but have also opened new avenues for comprehensive ecological assessments.
Looking ahead, the researchers plan to incorporate state-of-the-art attention mechanisms to further enhance the adaptability and contemporaneity of the proposed method. Recent technological advancements allows scientists to analyze vast amounts of data with unprecedented speed and precision, allowing for more informed decision-making in conservation management. Additionally, methodologies like few-shot/one shot learning and adaptative losses may improve models, particularly in discriminating fish with limited training data. With the ability to accurately estimate fish abundance in videos, researchers can now conduct more thorough and efficient monitoring of their populations. This is crucial not only for conservation efforts but also for understanding the intricate dynamics of marine ecosystems.
However, the authors stress that it is essential to acknowledge the challenges and limitations associated with this approach. While the results are promising, further validation and refinement are necessary to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the automated MaxN estimation method across different species and environments. Plus, there are ethical considerations that need to be taken into account regarding the use of AI in ecological research. As with any technology, there is a risk of unintended consequences, such as biases in data interpretation or the potential displacement of human involvement in scientific endeavors.
By combining technological innovation with ecological expertise, researchers are poised to make meaningful strides towards addressing the pressing challenges of biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation in our oceans. “Without a doubt, these novel AI-generated indicators would be immensely valuable to biologists, potentially revealing new insights into ecosystem functioning,” the authors conclude.

title: Council Post: Embracing Embodied AI: Surgical Robotics
text:
Dr. Joseph Nathan is the Co-Founder, President and Chief Medical Officer of ForSight Robotics, reshaping eyecare through surgical robotics.
Embodied AI—the integration of artificial intelligence with physical systems to perform complex tasks in real-world environments—is transforming how we interact with the world around us. By coupling AI-driven algorithms with robotics, especially in industries that require real-world solutions, we can enhance the human experience.
Various industries have already embraced embodied AI systems. Seeking to solve a global labor crisis driven by a shortage of at least 500,000 employees, which is projected to grow to a shortage of 2 million employees by 2030, the manufacturing and logistics industry has turned to AI-driven humanoid robots to fill jobs and replace the aging workforce globally. Companies like Symbotic and Boston Dynamics are pushing this technology forward. Enhanced by AI, these robots' abilities and efficacy have expanded significantly in the last decade.
In healthcare, to go beyond what is currently possible in complex dexterity tasks and unlock the full potential of quality surgical care, we must also embrace embodied AI. Creating synergy between robotics, AI and surgeons, surgical robotics can allow us to enhance precision and safety, provide better patient outcomes and reduce training costs. Elevating the level of care worldwide, surgical robotics are the next frontier for embodied AI.
AI-Driven Training Simulations
Simulations in medical education are crucial to the development of surgeons' skills, who require decades-long practice and experience to reach peak performance. Novice residents, mid-career surgeons and renowned surgical experts can benefit from AI-driven simulations to improve existing skills and develop new techniques that will provide better patient results.
AI-driven simulation training can improve surgical skills in a secure and risk-free environment while saving significant resources. It is inherently more efficient and accessible; instead of simulating surgical procedures on physical models (e.g., animal or cadaver models) and being bound by existing infrastructure (e.g., an operating room or procedure-specific tools), surgeons can practice their skills in virtual environments and from anywhere in the world.
At the heart of embodied AI is the utilization of data-driven insights to create training simulation models. AI-driven simulations can provide training for rare or complex cases that surgeons may only meet a handful of times over their career—but which would allow them to perfect the necessary techniques and be highly prepared for all scenarios in real time. Further, using the same interface as in real procedures, surgeons working with robotics systems can perform virtual simulated surgeries with the same console as in real surgery.
AI-driven simulations can also be brought into the physical world with virtual reality (VR) training. For example, the Johnson & Johnson Institute has introduced a global VR training program for surgeons and nurses, allowing OR staff to practice in an immersive environment. In the training program’s collaborative mode, healthcare professionals can also meet in the VR operating room—regardless of where they are physically located.
With VR-trained surgeons six times less likely to perform errors during real surgery than their peers training on real-world simulations, the higher skill transfer occurring between virtual simulation models and the OR is clearly evident. Coupled with robotics, AI-based simulations can expand access to top-tier surgical training while improving real-world outcomes.
Enhanced Visualization
With embodied AI, surgical robotics can integrate real-time imaging technologies to synthesize data and provide a wider and deeper understanding of the surgical field of view. Enhanced visualization can enable better decision making during operations while increasing the precision of each surgical step.
In ophthalmology, optical coherence tomography (OCT) technology (providing micron-level resolution of the eye) enables the integration of 3D imaging into the robotic system’s computer vision, significantly improving the accuracy and precision of each procedure, detecting potential residual fluids and avoiding unnecessary maneuvers. Combining augmented reality with state-of-the-art 3D imaging also provides surgeons with a more dynamic surgical arena.
Other physical platforms utilizing AI-driven visualization include unmanned aerial systems (UAS), which optimize the synergy between enhanced visualization and physical technologies. Powered by AI capabilities, their advanced vision systems allow them to navigate complex environments without risking human lives while processing real-time data to provide invaluable insights.
This includes search and rescue operations in challenging weather or terrain conditions, environmental protection or agricultural monitoring activities and intelligence gathering, among others.
Real-Time Guidance
Machine learning algorithms analyze vast amounts of preoperative and intraoperative data to assist in surgical planning and execution. These algorithms can predict potential complications, optimize surgical approaches and provide real-time feedback.
Robotic platforms with AI-driven imaging systems can create more detailed and real-time 3D "maps" of surgical sites, allowing surgeons to navigate complex anatomical structures with greater precision, improved safety and potentially better clinical outcomes.
Ultimately, embodied AI systems will be able to learn and adapt in real time during surgeries. By using sensory feedback to adjust their actions, AI-driven systems will be able to not just recommend but also adjust surgical plans based on a live feedback loop. By adapting to the real-world environment in the surgical arena and tracking real-time factors and changes, embodied AI platforms can truly transform surgery.
Maximizing The Potential Of Embodied AI
In the past five years, over $90 billion has been invested in new robotics startups—largely in the logistics, construction, medical, manufacturing and agriculture sectors—showing that the global need for embodied AI systems is backed by investors' confidence in the rising technology.
Coupling AI with physical systems can elevate real-world productivity and provide an answer to labor shortages across industries—while leveraging innovative technological capabilities and supporting a human-centered approach.
Empowered by AI, robotic surgery platforms provide a solution to a decreasing surgeon pool while expanding opportunities for surgeons worldwide to improve their surgical skills and, as such, perform more precise procedures. Integrating embodied AI in the surgical arena can transform quality healthcare and optimize the surgeon and patient experiences.
The time to embrace embodied AI technology is here. We must accelerate our technological progress and continue fueling the cycle of innovation as we strive to solve society’s biggest challenges.

title: Council Post: The Future Of Multimodal AI In Healthcare
text:
Amit Samsukha, Director & CTO at EmizenTech, is an e-commerce consultant, proficient at improvising IT infrastructure.
While the concept of multimodal AI has been gaining traction, many companies and users still don't understand the significance of this development.
While other types of AI can only handle a single data type at a time, what makes multimodal AI unique is that it can simultaneously manage various data from different sources—text, audio, video, images, etc.—to provide insights, generate content and predict upcoming situations.
For example, earlier iterations for ChatGPT were unimodal, but the more recent iterations are multimodal.
The multimodal AI market is expected to surge over the next several years with a CAGR of around 30% from 2024 to 2032. It is increasingly being adopted in diverse industries—from healthcare to automotive to finance—and the ability to harness multiple data modalities opens up many new possibilities.
This article will look at the role multimodal AI can play in healthcare, in particular, where it can help to better understand patient health by combining varied data sources into a singular view of patient data. Here are a few potential use cases and some insights into some of the challenges with multimodal AI.
1. Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
Multimodal AI can analyze data from diverse imaging techniques, which could help healthcare professionals offer more precise diagnoses. For example, by combining image data with patient records, genetic information and lab results, healthcare professionals should be able to gain a more comprehensive view to deliver more accurate diagnoses.
The ability to provide these insights could improve AI's ability to assist with everything from complex disease diagnosis to anomaly detection.
2. Drug Discovery
Multimodal AI can fuse information from biological data, molecular structures, clinical trials and other relevant sources to unveil complex patterns and links that traditional AI can't identify.
Furthermore, multimodal AI can predict drug effectiveness and possible side effects by analyzing multimodal data which should result in safer and more efficient clinical trials.
3. Personalized Treatment Plans
Multimodal AI can help craft personalized treatment plans integrating generic data, lifestyle details and clinical records. Further analyzing how different patients find medications by merging data from electronic health records (EHRs), clinical trials and real-world instances can also help to optimize drug prescriptions.
4. Patient Monitoring And Management
Multimodal AI can offer opportunities for improved continuous health monitoring by performing data processing coming from wearable devices and EHRs. This type of analysis should offer better support for chronic disease management for conditions like heart disease and diabetes.
Through analyzing patterns and trends in real-time data from past health records and wearables, healthcare providers and patients can receive early alerts to anticipate potential health problems.
5. Advanced Surgical Assistance
Multimodal AI models can also enhance AI-enabled AR systems by placing virtual information onto the surgical field to improve accuracy and safety. Integrating intra-operative data and real-time feedback from surgical instruments, for example, could help to diminish the risk of errors in complex surgeries.
Challenges Of Multimodal AI
Multimodal AI is a relatively new concept—even in the ever-evolving field of AI—and it is also more complex than traditional AI. Therefore, it introduces some new challenges and concerns that must be addressed, such as:
• Data Availability: Patient data may not always be available, but it is essential for multimodal AI to function.
• Data Privacy And Security: Maintaining patient data privacy and handling sensitive patient information may require new cybersecurity measures and privacy frameworks.
• Data Heterogeneity: Multimodal AI integrates data from various sources in different data formats, consistency and quality. This can be challenging for data handling.
• Clinical Adoption: Given its complexity, integrating multimodal AI solutions into clinical workflows will require careful training, planning and change management for seamless clinical adoption.
These challenges can be overcome by combining technical advancements, including building standardized data formats, aiming at easily explainable AI models. It will also require, like with other forms of AI, implementing appropriate security measures and creating ethical guidelines.
Also, AI experts, healthcare professionals and patients will need to collaborate to successfully implement and adopt multimodal AI in healthcare. As with everything in healthcare, this process could require several years of testing.
That said, if done correctly, integrating patient data from numerous sources has the potential to transform disease diagnosis, prevention, treatment and, ultimately, patient care. With multimodal AI, we can expect considerable advancements in patient care and better healthcare delivery.
